NEEDS_FIX: YES
<assessment>SOURCE shows a frontal elevation with a recessed ground-floor entrance, two stacked balconies, two-storey dark vertical cladding, a stepped brick frontage containing a tall divided window, and an upper glazed pavilion with thin projecting roof edges. CURRENT captures these principal elements, but compresses the ground storey and changes the tall window’s proportions and divisions. No source-backed primary volume is missing. SOURCE does not establish rear elevations, building depth or concealed roof construction; those CURRENT regions cannot establish fidelity. Visible balcony connections appear continuous, although screenshots alone cannot verify their underlying joints.</assessment>
<issue priority="1" view="front">problem: The ground storey is compressed. In the source-matched view, the distance from the main dark frontage beam to entrance ground level is roughly 15% shorter relative to the brick frontage above than in SOURCE. The boundary-wall tops also sit too close to that beam.
action: Locally increase the ground-storey height below the main beam, coordinating entrance glazing, doorway, steps and boundary-wall elevations while preserving the upper frontage proportions.</issue>
<issue priority="2" view="front">problem: The tall window in the right brick frontage is too narrow and stops too far above the frontage’s bottom beam. SOURCE shows four stacked glazed sections with central vertical divisions; CURRENT omits those divisions from the lower two sections.
action: Widen this opening locally, extend its lower end toward the beam, and restore the lower central mullions. Preserve its approximately correct head offset below the parapet.</issue>
<keep>Seven-bay vertical seam arrangement and intermediate horizontal joint in the dark left cladding.
Three upper glazing bays across the highest pavilion.
Two stacked glass-fronted balconies, with the lower balcony wider than the upper.
Thin dark projecting roof edge above the upper glazed pavilion.</keep>
